[agent] Progress ledger for the scheduled npm bug-hunt routine (label pm:npm).

Last updated: 2026-10-03 (run 10 with a ledger), main `045d7ec` (v5 + the #324/#326/#359/#403/#434/#454/#490/#516/#541 fixes and #570 API timeouts; the binary still reports 4.0.0), latest release v4.0.0 (previous v3.3.0, both from npm `@socketsecurity/socket-patch`). v5 makes hosted the default, removes `setup`, and makes hosted `rollback` re-resolve upstream registry entries. Cells marked (v4) were last verified on `f6b7fb9`.

## Coverage matrix

Cells are "pass", "fail #N" or "untested". Every cell uses a real npm install. Hosted cells use a local mock of the patch API with `--patch-server-url` pointed at it. Agent and vendored cells use the same mock or a hand-staged `.socket/`. "Cycle" means scan → fresh `npm ci` → `vex` → `rollback` byte-exact. "Suites" means `e2e_redirect_npm_build` + `e2e_vendor_npm_build` with `SOCKET_PATCH_NPM_E2E_REQUIRED=1`.

| OS | npm | Agent (apply / scan --mode agent) | Vendored | Hosted (v5 default) | Global `-g` (scan report / get+apply / vex / rollback) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linux | 6.14.18 | fail #356 (v4). pass: `-g` (v4) | pass: nested v2 lock (v4). v1 lock refused loudly (documented). fail #432 (alias mirror) | pass: v1-lock cycle (npm 6 installs the patched bytes), shrinkwrap-only v1 cycle. v1 alias: not wired (#432) | pass (v4) |
| Linux | 7.0.15 / 7.24.2 | pass: scan/apply, vex, `npm ci` → vex refuses, re-apply, rollback | pass: cycle + `--omit=dev`, workspaces, vendored↔hosted takeover, revert byte-exact | pass: cycle (alias, nested, dev), workspaces, takeovers | untested |
| Linux | 8.19.4 | fail #356 (v4). #403 / #516 closed by fixes | fail #432, **#588** (same-lock unwired copy). pass: cycle + `--omit=dev`, workspaces, takeovers, rescan no-op | pass: nested v2 cycle, shrinkwrap-only, workspaces, takeovers, rescan no-op, `overrides` (flat, alias, nested). fail #432 (alias mirror, npm 6 consumer), #490 (override over a git spec; closed by #491, not re-checked), **#588** (`--no-verify`) | untested |
| Linux | 9.9.4 | pass `-g` (v4); Node 18 cycle | pass: cycle + `--omit=dev` (main), Node 18 cycle | pass: cycle (alias, nested, dev), Node 18 cycle | pass (v4) |
| Linux | 10.8.2 (Node 18) / 10.9.x | pass: Node 18 cycle. fail **#554** (re-checked on `203e092`), **#356** (re-checked on `203e092`; alias-only scan now exits 0). pass: agent vex refuses a reverted nested copy (#516 fixed), bundled copy (both copies patched + vex) | pass: CRLF / BOM / tab layout cycle (#324 fixed), `--omit=dev`, agent↔vendored takeovers, rescan after a version bump (#541 fixed). fail **#588** (same-lock unwired copy) | pass: cycles (plain, alias, nested), `npm ci --omit=dev` + vex, shrinkwrapped `file:` dep, `JSONStream`, agent↔hosted takeovers, stale tree, lockfile-only, dry-run, rescan no-op, nested project (loud), `registry=` mirror, `.npmrc` variants, `overrides` (incl. `$ref`, nested object), policy (`--package`, `maxNewPatches`, `ignorePackages`, `minSeverity`), CRLF / BOM / tab / no-newline layout cycle. fail #325 (in-run `--vex` only, reopened), **#588** (`--no-verify` only; default `vex` refuses) | pass: all four, `--global-prefix`, `SOCKET_GLOBAL`, `--mode hosted` refused. fail #464 (report-only hint has no `-g`) |
| Linux | 11.20 / 11.21 | pass (v4); linked `.store` scoped transitive (11.21, #359 fixed). fail #403 (v4) | pass (v4). #490 (11.21; closed by #491, not re-checked) | pass: scoped, duplicate nested workspace copies, dual-lock drift, `omit-lockfile-registry-resolved`, `overrides`, `install-strategy=linked/nested/shallow` | untested |
| Linux | 12.1 / 12.2.0 | fail #356, **#554** (12.2.0) | fail **#588** (12.2.0). pass: hosted→vendored takeover + rollback, `--omit=dev`, workspaces, `remove` in a workspace, Node 26, `repair`, BOM+CRLF / tab cycle (12.2.0) | fail **#588** (`--no-verify`, 12.2.0). pass: `install-strategy=linked`, Node 26, `remove` in a workspace, `allow-remote=all` from env / user config still persisted, BOM+CRLF / tab cycle (12.2.0), workspace + alias cycle, dual-lock, drift, `npm install <pkg>` keeps the pin, path-scoped rollback, remove, `registry=` mirror, CRLF / spaced `.npmrc`. fail #433 | pass: all four |
| macOS | 10.9.7 | pass: linked `.store` apply/vex/rollback (main, #359 fixed). fail #356, #403 (v4) | pass: cycle + `--omit=dev`, revert (main) | pass: cycle, linked cycle (probe) | pass: all four (custom prefix) |
| macOS | 12.1.0 / 12.2.0 | pass: linked `.store` apply/vex/rollback (main, #359 fixed). fail #356, #403 (v4) | pass: cycle + `--omit=dev`, revert (main) | pass: cycle, linked cycle (probe) | pass: all four (custom prefix) |
| Windows | 10.9.7 | pass: linked `.store` apply/vex/rollback (main). fail #403 (v4) | pass: cycle + `--omit=dev`, revert (main) | pass: cycle, linked cycle (probe) | **fail #434** (default and custom prefix; `--global-prefix` works) |
| Windows | 12.1.0 / 12.2.0 | pass: linked `.store` apply/vex/rollback (main). fail #356, #403 (v4) | pass: cycle + `--omit=dev`, revert (main) | pass: cycle, linked cycle (probe) | **fail #434** |
| Windows 2022 | 10.9.7 / 12.2.0 | pass: linked `.store` apply/vex/rollback (main) | pass: cycle + `--omit=dev`, revert (main) | pass: linked cycle (probe) | **fail #434** |

## Agent writes through links (#626)

Agent mode follows a `node_modules` link into a workspace member, a `file:` dir or an `npm link` target, overwrites first-party source, and rollback restores upstream bytes. **fail #626** on Linux npm 6 (`file:`) / 8 / 10 / 12, macOS npm 10.9.7, and Windows npm 8 / 10 / 12, also on v4.0.0. Vendored refuses (`vendor_workspace_member`) and hosted skips with a warning: both pass.

## Backlog

0. **#626 follow-ups:** `apply --check` / `repair` over a link; a byte-identical fork (patched silently); a nested member's `node_modules` reached through a link.
1. **#588 follow-ups:** an unwired same-lock copy under `install-strategy=linked` and across a shrinkwrap/package-lock pair; whether `vendor --check` should flag it.
2. **Re-checks:** #325 (#432 still reproduces on `045d7ec`), #490 (override over URL / `file:` transitive deps on npm 8–12).
3. **#554 follow-ups:** agent `rollback` / `vex` with path policy over nested projects.
4. **#356:** alias-only agent `scan` now exits 0 with nothing applied (since #555). Watch for a fix.
5. **Maintainer request (global `-g`), still open:** npm 6/8/11 on macOS and Windows; an unwritable prefix (root-owned / `Program Files`); nvm, volta, fnm and Homebrew prefixes on macOS; `%APPDATA%\npm` now that #434 is closed. Full checklist in the 20261001T040000Z entry.
6. Stale probe branches the proxy can't delete (`git push --delete` fails with "remote end hung up" / "Everything up-to-date"): `bughunt/npm/20260930-alias-linked`, `20260930-win-mac-e2e`, `20260930-win-old-npm`, `20261001-crlf-paths`, `20261001-optional-dep`, `20261001-v5-hosted-global`, `20261001-win-global`, `20261002-v5-agent-vendored-winmac`, `20261003-ws-link-agent`, `20261003-ws-link-mac`. A maintainer needs to delete them.

## Known non-bugs

- `patches-api.socket.dev` is unreachable from the sandbox. Use hand-staged manifests, a local mock API, or the wiremock suites.
- Running `scan --mode hosted` from a workspace member directory finds no packages, because discovery is cwd-scoped. It's loud and writes nothing.
- An explicit `allow-remote` other than `all` is respected with a loud `redirect_npm_allow_remote` warning, and a fresh npm 12 install then fails EALLOWREMOTE (fails closed). This is documented.
- `npm update` re-resolves a hosted or vendored entry back to the registry. That's npm's behaviour; `vex` then refuses (`redirect_unwired` / `vendor_unwired`).
- After that, `apply` skips the package as "managed by `socket-patch vendor`" with exit 0 and doesn't take ownership back. That's by design (`apply.rs` `VENDOR_OWNED_MARKER`), and `vex` refuses.
- npm 12 doesn't install the dependencies of a `file:` directory dependency into the linked directory.
- The walk skips `build`, `dist`, `vendor`, `tmp`, `temp`, `coverage` and hidden directories, even when one is an npm workspace member (documented in docs/ecosystems.md).
- `apply` from a workspace member directory reports `noManifest` when `.socket/` lives at the root (`--cwd` scoping).
- Concurrent lock-taking commands fail fast with `lock_held` unless `--lock-timeout` is set (documented).
- `rollback` drops the rolled-back manifest entries and GCs their blobs unless `--preserve-state` is set (documented).
- Agent-mode `vex` omits patches (`ecosystem_not_setup`) when there's no `setup` hook and no `setup.manual` (documented).
- The VEX product `@id` is the raw origin URL for a non-GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket remote (documented in `vex --help`).
- npm ≥ 11 redacts UUID-shaped path segments in `npm root -g` stdout, so `apply -g` misses a global prefix whose path contains a UUID. That's npm's behaviour, it's loud (exit 1), and `--global-prefix` works around it. Not filed.
- The Windows + npm 6 suite cell needs `SOCKET_PATCH_NPM_E2E_LOCK_WRITER_BIN` (an npm ≥ 7 to write the v2 lock). That's a harness requirement.
- On Windows, npm/node can't run in a cwd longer than the Win32 limit, so deep-path cells there can't run.
- Hosted pins on any host other than `patch.socket.dev` or the `--patch-server-url` origin are invisible to `rollback`, `vex`, `list` and `remove` (documented). Mock runs must pass `--patch-server-url`.
- In the sandbox, hosted `rollback` can't reach registry.npmjs.org (the Rust client doesn't trust the proxy CA). Use `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY` pointed at a local passthrough.
- npm 6 installs the patched bytes from a hosted lockfileVersion 1 lock (measured on Linux, Node 22). npm-compatibility.md says it fails closed with EINTEGRITY; that's better than documented, not a bug.
- `rollback` re-adds `resolved` under `omit-lockfile-registry-resolved=true`: hosted keeps no ledger, and npm drops the field on its next install.
- A failed hosted lock write (an immutable lock) leaves `allow-remote=all` in `.npmrc`: exit 1, the documented mid-flush I/O residual.
- A bare hosted `scan` wires only the cwd project's lock. A nested non-workspace project warns `redirect_npm_entry_not_found`. `scan . sub` wires both, but `rollback` / `vex` from the root don't see `sub`'s pins (use `--cwd sub`).
- `rollback <path>` path targets select installed copies, so a workspace member whose dependency is hoisted to the root matches nothing (documented).
- Vendored `vex` attests from the committed artifact and only warns `vendored_tree_out_of_sync` when the live tree is stale (documented).
- `scan -g` without `-e` also scans the cargo, pypi and gem global stores (by design). `vex -g` outside a project needs `--product`.
- v5 removes `setup`, so the setup-hook cells are retired.
- Hosted `rollback` restores `resolved` to `registry.npmjs.org` (or `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY`) even when the project `.npmrc` uses a `registry=` mirror. That's documented ("default upstream registry entry"), and `npm ci` still works because of npm's `replace-registry-host`.
- `--package` and `ignorePackages` match package names and purls, not npm alias dependency keys (`lp@npm:left-pad` is matched by `left-pad`, not `lp`).
- npm 12 ignores `ALLOW-REMOTE=` and `allow_remote=` keys in `.npmrc`, so socket-patch appending `allow-remote=all` after them is correct.
- `minSeverity` skips patches whose per-package records carry no severity (documented). Mocks must fill `vulnerabilities` in `by-package`.
- `scan -g --mode agent` run inside a project records the global patch in the cwd `.socket/manifest.json`, and `rollback -g` drops it again. The manifest is cwd-scoped; CLI_CONTRACT "Global scope never touches the project's state" only covers hosted pins and the vendor ledger, and says rollback/remove `-g` "drop their manifest records".
- With no override, npm dedupes a root registry spec (`left-pad@1.3.0`) onto a transitive git copy of the same version, so the lock has a single git entry and the `redirect_npm_non_registry_entry_skipped` skip is correct.
- v4.0.0 agent `vex` omits patches with `ecosystem_not_setup` unless `setup.manual` lists the ecosystem (v4 behaviour). Set it when bisecting vex against v4.
- Hosted `vex` attests an omitted devDependency (`npm ci --omit=dev`) from its lock pin: documented ("With nothing installed … attests from that pin").
- A vendored v2 lock re-saved by npm 7/8 (`npm install`) loses `resolved` in the legacy `dependencies` mirror, because npm's serializer never writes it for a `file:` resolution. A cold-cache npm 6 `npm ci` then fails closed with EINTEGRITY. That's npm's behaviour; npm-compatibility.md's npm 6 + vendored v2 claim holds only until such a re-save.
- `vex` with a bundled (`inBundle`) copy refuses to attest (`patched_ref_unattributable`). In hosted mode the final error reads as "no references found" (exit 2) because a rejected reference keeps nothing alive (documented). Only the diagnostic is misleading.
- `scan --mode agent` over hosted pins keeps the pins and warns (`redirectState`; documented).
- npm vendored `scan --prune` / `vendor --revert` / `remove` keep (`keptVendoredEntries`, `vendor_artifact_kept`) an entry whose lock entry vanished after `npm uninstall` or a version bump. It's the deliberate drift-keep (pinned by `scan_prune_reverts_unused_vendored_entry`). Whether to reclaim it is an open maintainer question (#541 / PR #543 scope note). The rescan exit 1 is #541.
- `package-lock=false` in `.npmrc`: hosted pins are ignored by a plain `npm install` (unpatched), but `npm ci` honors the lock and `vex` refuses `not_applied`. Fails closed; the user's config choice.
- A symlinked `.npmrc` isn't written through (hosted warns that `allow-remote` must be set). A symlinked lock is refused `redirect_symlinked_file_unsupported`.
- Probe mock servers need a readiness loop: a scan that starts before the server listens fails with "tcp connect error: deadline has elapsed" (a probe artifact).

comments.body:
[agent] 2026-09-30: npm bug-hunt run

This is the first run with a ledger. An earlier run on the same day filed #324, #325 and #326 but wrote no entry.

**Tested:** main `f6b7fb9` (CLI 4.0.0). Latest release 4.0.0 and previous release 3.3.0, both from npm `@socketsecurity/socket-patch`. npm 6.14.18, 8.19.4, 10.9.7, 11.20.0 (installed, not yet exercised) and 12.1.0 on Node 22.22 (Linux). The probe added npm 10.9.4 and 12.1.0 on ubuntu, macOS and Windows.

**Setup:** the Socket patch API isn't reachable from the sandbox. Agent and vendored cells hand-stage `.socket/manifest.json` plus blobs (a marker prepended to `index.js`). Hosted cells use a ~60-line Python mock of the patch API: batch, by-package, the `patches/package` grant, `patches/view` and the tarball route, with the tarball gzipped with mtime 0 so the sha512 pin is stable across mock restarts. Every hosted cell ends with a fresh-checkout `npm ci` plus `vex`.

## Re-triage

#324, #325 and #326 are still open, their fix PRs (#337 and #345) aren't merged yet, and main is the same commit they were filed on. I didn't re-run them.

## Cells

- **Agent, npm alias** (`"lp": "npm:left-pad@1.3.0"`): **fail → #356** on npm 6, 8, 10 and 12, and on Linux, macOS and Windows. An alias-only project gets `package_not_installed`. A mixed project (plain + alias) patches only the plain copy, and `apply --vex` and `vex` attest `not_affected`. The same happens on 4.0.0 and 3.3.0. Vendored mode rewires the alias entry correctly.
- **Agent, `install-strategy=linked`** (`node_modules/.store`): **fail → #359** on npm 10 and 12, Linux, macOS and Windows. Transitive packages count as lockfile-only. `apply` exits 1, and `scan --apply` exits 0 with `success` while leaving them unpatched. `vendor` gets `package_not_installed`. Direct deps (symlinks) pass. It's the same on 4.0.0 and 3.3.0.
- **Agent, workspaces** (nested conflicting copies in two members): pass. **Agent, bundled copies:** pass (both copies patched).
- **Vendored, workspace nested lock entry** on npm 10 and 12: pass. Fresh `npm ci`, `npm install`, and `npm install <other> -w a` all keep the vendored entry.
- **Hosted, npm 12:** pass for a workspace member's nested entry with a fresh `npm ci` + `vex`; `.npmrc` auto-config with user-config `all` and env `all`; respected env `root` / user-config `none`, which warn loudly and fail closed with EALLOWREMOTE; `npm install` and `npm install <pkg>` keep the redirect on npm 10 and 12; after `npm update` unwires it, `vex` reports `redirect_unwired` and `rollback` removes the `.npmrc` cleanly.
- **setup:** pass. The postinstall + `dependencies` hooks re-patch nested workspace copies on `npm ci` (npm 10 and 12, via `npx` 4.0.0). A CRLF, tab-indented `package.json` with existing scripts round-trips byte-exact through `setup` / `setup --remove`. `apply --silent` on main prints nothing.

## Issues

- Filed #356: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/356 (npm aliases are never patched in agent mode, and VEX attests anyway)
- Filed #359: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/359 (`install-strategy=linked` `.store` copies are invisible, and `scan --apply` exits 0)
- Commented on both with the cross-OS probe results.

## False positives ruled out

- Hosted `scan` from a workspace member directory finds nothing: discovery is cwd-scoped, it's loud and writes nothing.
- An explicit non-`all` `allow-remote` is respected with a warning, and the install fails closed (documented).
- `npm update` dropping a hosted redirect is npm's own behaviour, and `vex` catches it.
- npm 12 doesn't install the dependencies of `file:` directory deps, so there's no copy to patch.
- An early hosted EINTEGRITY came from my mock: gzip mtime changed the tarball between restarts.
- 4.0.0's `apply --silent` token notice doesn't appear on main.

## Probe runs

- https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/actions/runs/36758644937 (alias + linked, 3 OS × npm 10.9.4 / 12.1.0). Its jobs are red only because the script's `bash -e` stopped at the expected failing `apply`.
- Deleting `bughunt/npm/20260930-alias-linked` failed (`git push --delete`: "remote end hung up"), so a maintainer needs to delete it.

## Next

1. Windows and macOS for vendored and hosted (autocrlf checkouts, long paths, drive-letter `file:` specs), using the mock API inside a probe.
2. Dual-lock (shrinkwrap + package-lock) drift after `npm install <pkg>` on npm 11 vs 12, and `patched_ref_unattributable`.
3. npm 9.x and 11.20.0 cells; Node 18 and 24 with npm 12.
4. `overrides` to an aliased spec in hosted and vendored modes (related to #356).
5. Concurrent `apply` runs, and an interrupted hosted run (`.npmrc` written, lock unchanged).

comments.body:
[agent] 2026-10-01: npm bug-hunt run

**Tested:** main `f6b7fb9` (CLI 4.0.0, unchanged since the last run). Latest release 4.0.0 and previous release 3.3.0 (npm `@socketsecurity/socket-patch`). npm 6.14.18, 8.19.4, 9.9.4, 10.9.7, 11.20.0 and 12.1.0 on Node 22.22 (Linux). Probes ran npm 10.9.7 and 12.1.0 on Node 24.15 on ubuntu, macOS (arm64) and Windows.

## Re-triage

Main hasn't moved, so #324, #325, #326, #356 and #359 still reproduce as filed, and I didn't re-run them. #326's fix PR #345 is still open; I built its head (see below).

## Cells

- **Real-npm suites** (`e2e_redirect_npm_build`, `e2e_vendor_npm_build`, `SOCKET_PATCH_NPM_E2E_REQUIRED=1`) on Linux with npm **9.9.4** and **11.20.0**: pass, 14/14 each.
- **Earlier probe runs found on the remote** (from the ledger-less first run on 2026-09-30, never recorded): runs 36731666366 and 36733259842. Both suites pass on Windows and macOS with npm 8.19.4, 10.9.9 and 12.1.0, and on macOS with npm 6. The only red cell is Windows + npm 6, where the harness found no npm ≥ 7 to write the v2 lock (`SOCKET_PATCH_NPM_E2E_LOCK_WRITER_BIN`). That's a harness limitation, not a bug.
- **Dual-lock (shrinkwrap + package-lock), vendored, npm 11 / 12:** pass. `npm install left-pad@1.3.0` on npm 12 reverts only package-lock.json, and on npm 11 only npm-shrinkwrap.json. In both cases `vex` refuses (`no_applicable_patches`), both with and without the manifest. A `vendor` re-run rewires both locks, and a fresh `npm ci` gets the patched bytes.
- **`overrides` to an aliased spec** (`"is-number": "npm:kind-of@6.0.3"`), vendored, npm 10/11/12: pass (`npm ci` and `npm install` keep the entry and install the patched bytes; `vex` is `not_affected`). Agent mode on that shape is #356's root cause.
- **Scoped alias** (`"@my/lp": "npm:left-pad@1.3.0"`), vendored, npm 11: pass, including a byte-exact `vendor --revert`.
- **Nested copy in a lockfileVersion 2 lock**, vendored, then `npm ci` with npm 6, 8 and 12: pass. The legacy `dependencies` mirror is rewired too.
- **Local `file:` tarball dep**, vendored, npm 8/10/11/12: **fail**. That's #326, so I added a comment instead of filing. PR #345's head refuses it with `vendor_lock_entry_not_rewritable`.
- **Global (`apply -g`)** with `npm_config_prefix` / `--global-prefix`, npm 6/9/11/12: pass.
- **`node_modules` as a symlink** to a directory outside the project: apply and rollback pass.
- **Concurrent `apply` ×6:** exactly one wins and the rest get `lock_held` (documented fail-fast default). A stale `apply.lock` and a SIGKILLed holder don't block the next run.
- **`setup` on npm 11 with a workspace:** pass (both root and member hooks; the root copy is re-patched on `npm ci`).
- **Probe `20261001-crlf-paths`** (run 36796395924), 3 OS × npm 10/12, under a space + unicode path: a vendored project committed with LF and cloned with `core.autocrlf=true` passes `npm ci` (patched) and `vex` (`not_affected`), and a vendor re-run is a no-op. `vendor --revert` drops the CRLF (#324). Agent mode with a CRLF manifest: apply and rollback pass. A deep path (~270 characters) passes on Linux and macOS; on Windows, npm itself can't run there (Win32 cwd limit).
- **Platform-skipped optional dependency:** **fail → #403.** When every manifest patch targets an optional package the host doesn't install (`fsevents`, `@esbuild/*`), `apply` exits 1, so the `setup` hook fails `npm ci` and `npm install`. It reproduces on Linux with npm 8/10/11/12 and in probe `20261001-optional-dep` (run 36796693378) on all 3 OSes × npm 10/12. 4.0.0 and 3.3.0 do the same. With one installed patch alongside, it's only a warning and exits 0.

## Issues

- Filed #403: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/403
- Commented on #326 (`file:` tarball variant, and PR #345 verified): https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/326#issuecomment-5922216975

## False positives ruled out

- `apply` skipping an unwired vendored package as "managed by `socket-patch vendor`" (exit 0) after the lock is reverted is by design: apply never takes ownership back from vendor, and `vex` refuses.
- `rollback` removing the manifest entries and GCing their blobs is documented (README command table).
- Agent-mode `vex` exits 1 with `ecosystem_not_setup` when there's no `setup` hook or `setup.manual`. That's documented.
- The VEX product `@id` is the raw origin URL for a non-GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket remote, which is documented (`vex --help`).
- npm ≥ 11 redacts UUID-shaped path segments in `npm root -g` output (`/tmp/***/…`), so `apply -g` misses a global prefix whose path contains a UUID (loud: `package_not_installed`, exit 1). That's npm's output redaction, and rare; not filed. A workaround exists (`--global-prefix`).
- The Windows deep-path failure comes from npm/node themselves, not socket-patch.

## Probe branches

- `bughunt/npm/20261001-crlf-paths`, `bughunt/npm/20261001-optional-dep`. `git push --delete` prints "Everything up-to-date" through the proxy and deletes nothing, for these and for the three 2026-09-30 branches (`20260930-alias-linked`, `20260930-win-mac-e2e`, `20260930-win-old-npm`). **A maintainer needs to delete all five.**

## Next

1. Hosted mode on macOS and Windows with the `.npmrc` allow-remote auto-config (the suites pass; probe user-config `none` and env overrides there).
2. `npm ci --omit=optional` / `--omit=dev` against a manifest that patches an omitted package (likely the same root cause as #403; check vendored and hosted too).
3. Node 18 with npm 9/10, and npm 12 on Node 26.

[agent] 2026-10-01: maintainer note: test global (`-g`) mode for hosted patches

This is a maintainer request, not a run report. Add it to the top of the backlog and keep it there until the cells below are covered.

**Ask:** make sure we correctly scan global installs when `-g` / `--global` is passed, on every major npm version and on Linux, macOS and Windows.

**Where npm puts global installs:** `npm install -g`; discovery via `npm root -g`. Cover the default prefix, a user prefix (`npm config set prefix`), nvm / volta / fnm / Homebrew node, and Windows `%APPDATA%\npm`. Known: npm ≥ 11 redacts UUID path segments in `npm root -g`, so `--global-prefix` is needed there.

**What to check** (prove each with a real global install, not by reading source):
1. `socket-patch scan -g` (no `--mode`) is report-only. It must find every globally installed npm package that has a hosted patch: none missing, no project packages leaking in, correct versions. Also check `--json`.
2. `scan -g` run from inside a npm project versus outside one: `-g` must scan only the global location, and a scan without `-g` must never touch it.
3. `scan -g --mode hosted` and `scan --global-prefix <dir> --mode hosted` must refuse loudly, as designed ("global installs have no project lockfile to redirect"). They must exit non-zero and write nothing.
4. `get -g` defaults to agent mode. Check `scan -g --apply`, `apply -g`, `rollback -g` and `vex -g`: the globally installed copy is actually patched (run the installed tool or import it), rollback restores it byte for byte, and `vex` only attests what's applied.
5. `--global-prefix <dir>` and `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1` behave the same as `-g`. That covers custom prefixes, version managers, paths with spaces or unicode, and a non-root user's prefix.
6. A global directory you can't write to (root-owned prefix, Windows Program Files) must fail loudly with a clear error, never exit 0 unpatched.

Add OS × npm version cells for `-g` (scan report / apply / rollback) to the coverage matrix, and use probe branches for macOS and Windows.

[agent] 2026-10-01: handover from the Deno bug-hunt routine (ledger #308): agent-mode `vex` attests not_affected while other nested copies of the same name@version are unpatched

Found while testing Deno's hoisted linker. The root cause is generic npm-family, and the realistic trigger is plain npm, so this is yours to file. Nothing was filed from Deno. I searched for duplicates (#325, #405, #435, #471 are bundled / hosted / isolated / global variants) and found none covering agent mode.

**Defect.** In agent mode `vex` hashes only the **first** installed copy of each PURL: `crates/socket-patch-cli/src/commands/vex.rs:556` `let package_paths = collapse_to_first(copies.clone());`. Every other copy is ignored, while hosted-basis PURLs check every copy (`vex_consumed`). CLI_CONTRACT's verification table says agent evidence is "the installed tree". When the first copy is patched and another copy of the same `name@version` isn't, vex emits `not_affected` for a package whose unpatched copy is still loaded at runtime. The verdict depends on crawl order: revert the first copy instead and vex correctly says `not_applied`.

**Realistic trigger (real npm 10.9.4, main `61cfb9b`, Linux, reproduced 2/2).** `apply` patches every copy present, then a later `npm install` of new dependents extracts fresh, unpatched nested copies and leaves the old patched one alone:

```sh
mkdir npmdup && cd npmdup && echo '{"name":"npmdup","version":"1.0.0"}' > package.json
npm install kind-of@6.0.3 is-number@3.0.0          # nests kind-of@3.2.2 under is-number
# offline manifest + blobs patching package/index.js of pkg:npm/kind-of@3.2.2 (any free patch works)
socket-patch apply --offline                         # applied 1
npm install is-accessor-descriptor@0.1.6             # adds node_modules/is-accessor-descriptor/node_modules/kind-of@3.2.2 (unpatched)
socket-patch vex --offline -O v.json                 # exit 0, 1 statement: not_affected pkg:npm/kind-of@3.2.2
```

Copies afterwards: `is-number/node_modules/kind-of` patched, `is-accessor-descriptor/node_modules/kind-of` **unpatched**. A re-run of `apply` does patch the new copies (`applied: 2, skipped: 1`), so apply is fine; only vex is wrong.

**Deno too:** `nodeModulesLinker: "hoisted"` (2.9.7) with `kind-of@6.0.3` + `is-number@3.0.0` + `is-accessor-descriptor@0.1.6` gives two nested `kind-of@3.2.2` copies. Reverting the `is-accessor-descriptor` copy → vex `not_affected`. Reverting the `is-number` copy → `not_applied`. Same crawl-order dependence. It's likely the same for yarn classic, bun hoisted and pnpm (multiple `.pnpm` peer variants of one version).

Expected: agent vex attests a PURL only when every installed copy the crawler finds verifies (the hosted path already does this), otherwise it omits it as `not_applied` / `hash_mismatch`.

- agent `scan --mode agent` under `install-strategy=linked` patches all 4 `.store` copies, then `vex` and `rollback` (#359's fix confirmed on macOS and Windows);
- the vendored cycle, including `npm ci --omit=dev`, `vex`, and a byte-exact `vendor --revert` with no artifacts left behind;
- the hosted linked cycle with `vex`.

The branch delete failed through the proxy again ("remote end hung up"), so it joins the stale-branch list.

## Cells (Linux unless noted)

- **Hosted `npm ci --omit=dev` + `vex`** (npm 10): pass. The omitted devDependency is attested from its lock pin, which CLI_CONTRACT documents ("With nothing installed … attests from that pin").
- **Vendored cycle with `--omit=dev`**, nested copy, revert: pass on npm 7.0.15, 7.24.2, 8.19.4, 9.9.4, 10.9.4, 11.21.0, 12.2.0 (Node 24 and 26). On npm 6 with a v1 lock it refuses loudly with `vendor_lockfile_version_unsupported`, which is documented.
- **Hosted cycle** (alias, nested, devDependency, byte-exact rollback): pass on npm 7.0.15, 7.24.2, 9.9.4, and 12.2.0 on Node 26.
- **Workspaces** (a member's nested copy, root + member deps), vendored and hosted: pass on npm 7.0.15, 7.24.2, 8.19.4, 10, 12.
- **`npm-shrinkwrap.json` as the only lock**, hosted: pass on npm 6 (v1) and npm 8 (v2).
- **A `file:` tarball dependency that ships its own `npm-shrinkwrap.json`** (its nested copy pinned by it), hosted, with `npm ci` and `npm install`: pass.
- **Mixed-case legacy name** (`JSONStream`), hosted cycle: pass.
- **npm 12 hosted with `install-strategy=linked`**: pass. Rollback leaves `allow-remote=all` in a mixed `.npmrc` (documented `npm_allow_remote_left`).
- **`allow-remote=all` already set** in the env var or `~/.npmrc` when scanning: the project `.npmrc` is still written, so teammates' npm 12 `npm ci` works. Pass.
- **Takeovers** vendored↔hosted (npm 7.24.2, 8.19.4, 12) and agent↔hosted/vendored (npm 10): pass, byte-exact undo. hosted→agent keeps the pins with a loud warning plus `redirectState` (documented).
- **Rescan idempotency** (vendored and hosted, npm 8 and 12): pass, nothing rewritten.
- **`remove <purl>`** for a member's nested copy in a workspace, hosted and vendored on npm 12: pass.
- **Agent cycle on npm 7.0.15 / 7.24.2:** apply, `vex`, `npm ci` (`vex` then refuses), re-apply and rollback: pass.
- **A bundled (`inBundle`) copy of a vendored or hosted patch:** pass. `vex` refuses to attest (`patched_ref_unattributable`). The hosted variant's final error then says "no hosted or vendored patch references were found … Run `socket-patch scan` first" (exit 2), although the warning just above names the rejected reference. That follows the documented rule that a rejected mention keeps nothing alive. Only the diagnostic is misleading, so I didn't file it.

## Issues

None filed, commented on or closed. Nothing new met the bar.

## False positives ruled out

- **npm 7/8 `npm install` re-save drops `resolved` from vendored entries in the v2 legacy `dependencies` mirror.** A cold-cache npm 6 `npm ci` of that lock then fails EINTEGRITY (fails closed). npm's own serializer never writes `resolved` for a `file:` resolution (`@npmcli/arborist/lib/shrinkwrap.js` `_buildLegacyLockfile`, npm 8.19.4 lines 1028-1038), so socket-patch can't keep it. npm-compatibility.md's "npm 6 DOES install a vendored v2 lock from its legacy mirror" holds only until npm 7+ re-saves the lock. A warm npm 6 cache still installs the patched bytes (integrity-keyed).
- A hosted pin attesting an omitted devDependency: documented (see above).

5. Agent `vex` with duplicate copies across workspace members (#516 follow-up).

```
repo/ (.git, package.json + package-lock.json: left-pad@1.3.0)
  apps/web/       bun.lock  is-number@6.0.0
  apps/api/       bun.lock  is-odd@3.0.1
  services/legacy bun.lock  left-pad@1.3.0, is-number@6.0.0
  tests/e2e/      bun.lock  is-number@6.0.0
socket.yml: version: 2 / patches: ignorePaths: ["/services/"]

```
- Result: `success`, `policy.counts {filtered: 0, retained: 0}`, and `services/legacy/node_modules/left-pad/index.js` is patched.

[agent] 2026-10-02: handover from the Bun bug-hunt routine (#306). Not filed: the behaviour lives in the shared npm-family VEX discovery and reproduces identically with npm 10, so it isn't Bun-specific. It might also be by design, since CLI_CONTRACT's vendored row attests from "the committed artifact + lock wiring".

**Observation:** a vendored (and, under `--no-verify`, a hosted) `vex` attests `not_affected` for `name@version` when the lockfile wires one copy of it to the Socket artifact and a second, plain **registry** entry of the same `name@version` in the **same** lockfile is left unwired. That second copy installs unpatched. `contest_across_locks` (`vex/discover/mod.rs:574`) and `push_uncontested` (`vex/discover/npm.rs:99`, `*j != i`) only contest refs across *different* locks. #325 / #326 / #497 handle bundled and non-registry copies in the same lock, but not an unwired registry copy.

**A natural way to get there:** run vendored (or hosted) scan, then add a workspace member that depends on the same `name@version` and run `npm install` / `bun install`. The package manager resolves the new nested copy from the registry. Re-running `scan` heals it (verified), but in between `vex` attests.

Repro (main `61cfb9b`, Linux, 2/2 runs each, local mock API; the patch is for `pkg:npm/is-number@6.0.0`):
```sh
# root: is-number@7.0.0, workspaces packages/*; packages/a: is-number@6.0.0
npm install && socket-patch scan --mode vendored --yes        # packages/a/node_modules/is-number → file:.socket/vendor/…
# add packages/b with is-number@6.0.0
npm install                                                    # packages/b/node_modules/is-number → registry 6.0.0 (unpatched bytes)
socket-patch vex --json --product pkg:npm/app@1.0.0 -O vex.json   # verified pkg:npm/is-number@6.0.0 (also with --no-verify)
```
Bun (1.4.2, text v2 workspace lock): the same with `c/is-number: ["is-number@6.0.0", "", {}, …]` beside the rewired entries. Vendored `vex` (default and `--no-verify`) attests. Hosted default `vex` correctly skips it (it hashes the installed copies), but hosted `vex --no-verify` attests. Bun 1.1.45 `bun.lockb`: hosted default skips, which is correct.

**Expected (suggestion):** treat an unwired registry entry of the same `name@version` in the same lock like the #326 non-registry case: no attestation, plus a diag ("re-run scan to rewire every copy").

## Backlog

0. **Maintainer request (global `-g` mode):** the Linux cells are done. Still to do: macOS and Windows (corepack, standalone and npm-installed pnpm; `PNPM_HOME` with spaces or unicode; Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\pnpm`), and an unwritable prefix as a non-root user. Full checklist in the 20261001T040000Z entry. Needs a probe branch.
1. Delete the stale probe branch `bughunt/pnpm/20260930-virtual-store`. `git push --delete` failed through the git proxy in runs 1, 3 and 10, and was denied by the permission policy in runs 2, 5–9 and 11, so a maintainer needs to do it. macOS and Windows probes stay on hold until branch cleanup works.
2. #636 follow-ups: a hosted → vendored takeover with several packages, then revert, and a user-created `pnpm` table with several vendored packages.
3. #362 GVS transitive and #435 global `-g`: re-check exit codes under #555's skip semantics on 11.28.3 / 12.8.1.
4. Rush subspaces (`common/config/subspaces/*`), and Rush + pnpm 8 / 10.
5. `pnpm patch-commit` after a hosted pin, then rollback. `package-import-method=clone` on reflink (needs CI).
6. #556 follow-ups: merging branch lockfiles after a hosted pin, and agent `vex` on the branch.
7. Re-verify #360, #362, #435, #466, #492, #556, #557, #590, #601 (PR #605), #633 and #636 when fixes land.
8. Vendored on Windows and macOS (autocrlf: expect the `vendor_lockfile_crlf_unsupported` refusal; check that hosted handles the same checkout).

## Known non-bugs

- `patches-api.socket.dev` and (for the Rust client) `registry.npmjs.org` are unreachable from the sandbox. Mock the API and point `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY` at a mirror.
- v5 recognises hosted pins only on the configured patch server. Against a mock without `SOCKET_PATCH_SERVER_URL`, `rollback` says "Manifest not found". That's a fixture artifact.
- v5 hosted rollback and takeover keep a user-edited `trustLockfile: true` and warn `pnpm_trust_lockfile_left`. A workspace file that exactly matches hosted mode's scaffold is deleted, including a user's own `packages: ['.']` file that the trust append made identical to it (CLI_CONTRACT, upstream restore).
- pnpm 10 ignores `enableGlobalVirtualStore` when `CI` is set, so the global-virtual-store cells don't engage on GH runners with pnpm 10.
- pnpm 12 (and 11) ignore `.npmrc` for `virtual-store-dir` / `enable-global-virtual-store`. Put them in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, or in the global `config.yaml`.
- pnpm 11+ `pnpm root -g` / `pnpm add -g` fail unless `$PNPM_HOME/bin` is on `PATH`. Put it there in fixtures.
- Vendored refusals that are intended, loud and fail-closed: a CRLF `pnpm-lock.yaml` or `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`vendor_lockfile_crlf_unsupported`), a BOM package.json (`vendor_pkg_json_unsupported`), an inline / flow `overrides:` mapping (`vendor_override_conflict`, unit-tested), and `patchedDependencies` on the target (`vendor_lock_entry_unsupported`; the detail wrongly says "peer-suffixed snapshot key", which is cosmetic).
- Vendored `vex` attests from the committed artifact plus lock wiring even when the tree isn't installed. That's by design (CLI_CONTRACT "Manifest-less VEX").
- `vex -g` needs `--product` outside a project ("Could not auto-detect a top-level product PURL").
- Agent-mode `get <purl>` for an uninstalled package reports `success, applied: 1` when another manifest entry applies. The nested apply fails only when nothing matches. It's not pnpm-specific (noted on #362).
- A compact single-line `package.json` comes back 2-space-indented after vendor + rollback. There's no indent to detect, and indented files round-trip byte-exactly, so it's cosmetic.
- Hosted on pnpm 9 over an existing upstream `node_modules`: a frozen install keeps the upstream bytes. That's documented in the `redirect_pnpm_trust_lockfile` warning, and VEX doesn't attest it.
- pnpm 12 warns that `package.json` `pnpm.overrides` is ignored on vendored projects. The workspace-file override is what takes effect, so this is noise only.
- A `vex --output /dev/stdout` hang when stdout is a pipe is not pnpm-specific.
- Vendored refuses pnpm catalogs (`catalogs:` entry) and peer-suffixed snapshot keys with `vendor_lock_entry_unsupported` ("this lock shape is not supported yet"). It's loud and writes nothing. Hosted handles both.
- pnpm 10's `configDependencies` copy (`node_modules/.pnpm-config/`) stays unpatched under hosted mode while VEX attests the regular copy. Config deps run only at install time, and pnpm 10 keeps their integrity in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
- On v5, vendoring always downloads its artifact from the patch service (`--vendor-source build` was removed), so offline vendoring with only a staged manifest fails with `vendor_service_offline_conflict`. Fixtures need the mock grant to match the manifest UUID.
- `rush update --full` re-resolves the Rush lock and drops the hosted pin, like `pnpm update`. VEX then honestly reports nothing to attest.
- pnpm 9.15.9's frozen install fails on its own unmodified lock when a workspace uses `dependenciesMeta.injected` ("importer dependencies meta (undefined) doesn't match"). That's upstream pnpm, not socket-patch.
- Old pnpm needs an old Node (≤ 6 needs Node 16, ≤ 2 needs Node 10), and pnpm 3 takes `--store` rather than `--store-dir`. Fixture notes.
- Agent apply over a pnpm `patchedDependencies` edit to the same file overwrites it with the verified patched content and warns `content_mismatch_overwritten` (documented default mismatch policy; `--strict` refuses). Hosted composes both patches, and `vex` then declines (`no_applicable_patches`), because the file matches neither hash.
- Hosted on pnpm 11/12 respects an explicit `trustLockfile: false` (any YAML spelling) and warns `redirect_pnpm_trust_lockfile` with the remedy. The following frozen install fails, which is documented.
- Vendored refuses pnpm ≤ 6 locks (5.x up to 5.3) with `vendor_lockfile_version_unsupported`, and pnpm 7/8 workspace locks with `vendor_lock_entry_unsupported`. pnpm 7/8 vendored locks carry an absolute `file:` specifier (`vendor_pnpm_legacy_absolute_specifier`), so a moved checkout needs `pnpm install --offline --no-frozen-lockfile` once. Both are documented.
- pnpm 11+ ignores `package.json` `pnpm.patchedDependencies`. Put it in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
- A dead-registry fresh install fails when the fixture has any unpatched dependency (it still needs the registry). Use the live registry for those fixtures, or patch every dependency.
- Vendored from a workspace member cwd fails closed with `vendor_lockfile_missing` (`partial_failure`). Hosted's silent success in the same layout is #590.
- A `package.json` without a trailing newline gains one after vendor + revert. That's a fixture artifact; files that end in a newline round-trip byte-exactly.
- Bundled-copy fixtures need a registry-served host package. A `file:` tarball host (`.pnpm/bundler@file+…`) is patched correctly, so it doesn't reproduce #601.

[agent] 2026-09-30: pnpm bug-hunt run

**Tested:** main `f6b7fb9` (CLI 4.0.0 workspace version), latest release 4.0.0 (previous 3.3.0, both installed from npm for comparison). pnpm 7.33.7, 8.15.9, 9.15.9, 10.0.0, 10.5.2, 10.12.1, 10.34.5, 11.27.0, 12.4.2 and 12.8.1 (the current `latest`), on Node 22 in the sandbox. Patch data is a hand-staged `.socket/manifest.json` plus blobs (agent and vendored mode) and a local Python mock of the patch API and tarball routes (hosted mode). No secrets.

This is the first run: no earlier ledger, and no open `pm:pnpm` issues to re-triage.

### Cells
- **fail #361**: agent `apply` / `rollback` with `enableGlobalVirtualStore`. Writes land in the shared `<store>/links` dir: an unrelated project is patched, and one project's rollback unpatches another. Fails on Linux with pnpm 10.12.1–12.8.1, and on the macOS and Windows probe with pnpm 11.27.0 and 12.8.1. Releases 3.3.0 and 4.0.0 behave the same.
- **fail #362**: agent `apply` on a transitive dep with a custom `virtualStoreDir` (pnpm 8–12) or the global virtual store (10.12+) is reported `package_not_installed`. Fails on Linux, macOS and Windows.
- **fail #360**: vendored mode on pnpm 10.5.2, 10.12.1 and 10.34.5 with user `overrides:` in pnpm-workspace.yaml. `vendor` succeeds, then a fresh `--frozen-lockfile` install fails with `ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH`, and a re-lock drops the user's overrides. Passes on 10.0.0, 11.27.0 and 12.8.1. Release 4.0.0 has the same bug.
- pass: vendored lifecycle on pnpm 10.34.5 and 11.27.0 (vendor → fresh frozen `--offline` install → vex → revert). Also passes with `nodeLinker: hoisted` and with a flow `packages: ['.']` plus `catalog: {…}`.
- pass: agent `apply` / `rollback` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` (pnpm 11.27.0). The CAS file is not written through.
- pass: hosted `scan --mode hosted` on pnpm 11.27.0 against the mock API: fresh frozen install with an empty store gets the patched bytes. trustLockfile handling passes for CRLF, no-EOL and trailing-comment `trustLockfile: true` workspace files.
- fail, not filed (queued in the backlog): hosted trustLockfile append and vendored overrides append on a *whole-document flow* `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`{packages: [.]}`) or a file ending in `...`. The command reports success, then pnpm can't parse the file ("end of the stream or a document separator is expected"). Reproduced on pnpm 11.27.0.
- refused, as designed: vendored with a CRLF `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or `pnpm-lock.yaml` (`vendor_lockfile_crlf_unsupported`), a BOM package.json (`vendor_pkg_json_unsupported`), inline `overrides: {}` / `{x: y}` (`vendor_override_conflict`, covered by the `inline_workspace_overrides_mapping_is_refused` unit test), and `patchedDependencies` on the target (`vendor_lock_entry_unsupported`).

### Issues
- Filed #360, #361 and #362.

### False positives ruled out
- Vendored `vex` attesting `not_affected` in a fresh clone whose install failed is by design: vendored VEX stands on the committed artifact plus lock wiring (CLI_CONTRACT "Manifest-less VEX"; `vendored_tree_out_of_sync` is a warning only).
- The global virtual store "not reproducing" with pnpm 10.34.5 on GH runners is expected: pnpm 10 disables it when `CI` is set. pnpm 11+ keeps it.
- `vex --output /dev/stdout` hangs when stdout is a pipe. It's not pnpm-specific, so it wasn't filed here; it's noted for whoever owns the CLI.

### Probe
- `bughunt/pnpm/20260930-virtual-store`, run https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/actions/runs/36759597534 (ubuntu, macos and windows × pnpm 10.34.5, 11.27.0 and 12.8.1). **The branch could not be deleted:** the git proxy dropped `git push --delete` three times ("unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet"). A maintainer needs to delete it.

### Next
1. Flow-style or `...`-terminated `pnpm-workspace.yaml` breaking under the hosted trust append and the vendored overrides append. Confirm on pnpm 10 and 12, then file.
2. Hosted mode on pnpm 7/8 (lock 5.4/6.0) workspaces with catalogs, and peer-suffixed instances with the mock API. Then Rush/subspace locks.
3. The vendored takeover (hosted → vendored → hosted) on pnpm 11/12, plus `rollback` byte-exactness of `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
4. Agent `apply` with `injected` workspace deps (`dependenciesMeta.injected`) and `package-import-method=clone/copy`.
5. pnpm 1–6 legacy layouts (`node_modules/.registry.npmjs.org`, pnpm 4/5 nested host dirs) on Node 16 for agent mode.

[agent] 2026-10-01: maintainer note: test global (`-g`) mode for hosted patches

This is a maintainer request, not a run report. Add it to the top of the backlog and keep it there until the cells below are covered.

**Ask:** make sure we correctly scan global installs when `-g` / `--global` is passed, on every major pnpm version and on Linux, macOS and Windows.

**Where pnpm puts global installs:** `pnpm add -g`; discovery via `pnpm root -g` (`PNPM_HOME`). Cover pnpm 7–10 global-dir layouts, the global virtual store, and pnpm installed through corepack, standalone and npm.

**What to check** (prove each with a real global install, not by reading source):
1. `socket-patch scan -g` (no `--mode`) is report-only. It must find every globally installed pnpm package that has a hosted patch: none missing, no project packages leaking in, correct versions. Also check `--json`.
2. `scan -g` run from inside a pnpm project versus outside one: `-g` must scan only the global location, and a scan without `-g` must never touch it.
3. `scan -g --mode hosted` and `scan --global-prefix <dir> --mode hosted` must refuse loudly, as designed ("global installs have no project lockfile to redirect"). They must exit non-zero and write nothing.
4. `get -g` defaults to agent mode. Check `scan -g --apply`, `apply -g`, `rollback -g` and `vex -g`: the globally installed copy is actually patched (run the installed tool or import it), rollback restores it byte for byte, and `vex` only attests what's applied.
5. `--global-prefix <dir>` and `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1` behave the same as `-g`. That covers custom prefixes, version managers, paths with spaces or unicode, and a non-root user's prefix.
6. A global directory you can't write to (root-owned prefix, Windows Program Files) must fail loudly with a clear error, never exit 0 unpatched.

Add OS × pnpm version cells for `-g` (scan report / apply / rollback) to the coverage matrix, and use probe branches for macOS and Windows.

  - **fail #466 (new)**: vendored on the two-doc lock refuses with `vendor_lock_entry_not_found`. A project vendored first and turned two-doc later breaks on every unwind. `vendor --revert` exits 0 with `success`, rollback reports `vendoredKept` "left untouched", and the default `scan` takeover exits 0 having deleted the ledger. All three leave 5 `file:.socket/vendor` refs, so the next frozen install fails with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`. Root cause: `section_bounds` takes the first `packages:` / `importers:` header. - **fail #518 (new):** in a Rush repo (pnpm 9.15.9 lock 9.0, and 8.15.9 lock 6.0), the npm crawler skips `common/temp` (`SKIP_DIRS` has `"temp"`). Transitive deps installed in `common/temp/node_modules/.pnpm` therefore show as `notInstalled`. After `scan --mode hosted` pins `common/config/rush/pnpm-lock.yaml`, `vex` attests `not_affected` from the lockfile basis while the installed store copy is still upstream. With `preventManualShrinkwrapChanges: true`, `rush install` refuses until `rush update`, as documented. The pin survives `rush update`. A cold `rush install`, a warm one, and `rush install --purge` all install the patched bytes. `vex` attests correctly once the tree is patched.

Hosted then exits `success` / `redirected: 0` with only `redirect_pnpm_no_lockfile`, and the member lock stays unpinned. Reproduced 2/2. https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/492#issuecomment-5943308968
- pass: legacy layouts. Agent apply and rollback on a transitive dep (Node loads the patched copy), plus hosted pin → fresh frozen install with an empty store → byte-exact rollback, all pass on:
  - pnpm 2.25.7 (`shrinkwrap.yaml`, `node_modules/.registry.npmjs.org/…`)
  - pnpm 3.8.1 (lock 5.1, same layout)
  - pnpm 4.14.4 (lock 5.1, `.pnpm/registry.npmjs.org/<name>/<ver>`)
  - pnpm 5.18.10 (lock 5.2)
  - pnpm 6.35.1 (lock 5.3)

- pass: hosted with `dependenciesMeta.injected` on 8.15.9 / 12.8.1.

comments.author: github-actions
comments.body:
[agent] Handover from the npm bug-hunt routine (#302): agent mode writes through workspace links into first-party source

Filed as **#626** (pm:npm): https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/626

With npm, agent-mode `scan`/`apply` follows a `node_modules/<name>` symlink that points at a workspace member, a `file:` directory or an `npm link` target whenever that local package's `name@version` matches a patched registry package. The default mismatch policy then overwrites the user's own `index.js` with the upstream patched file. `vex` attests it, and `rollback` writes the upstream *original* over the user's code. Vendored mode refuses the same case (`vendor_workspace_member`).

The suspect code is shared by the whole npm family: `crates/socket-patch-core/src/crawlers/npm_crawler.rs:1933` `acceptable_package_entry` accepts any symlink in an importer tree. pnpm links `workspace:` deps and `link:` / `file:` dirs the same way, so the pnpm routine may want to check:
- a pnpm workspace member named `left-pad`, version `1.3.0`, depended on via `workspace:*`
- a `link:../fork` dependency

with `socket-patch scan --mode agent` against a mock patch for `left-pad@1.3.0`. If it reproduces, add a comment to #626 rather than filing a duplicate.

Repro script (npm): see the issue body.

Warm-cache frozen install: 1.0.2 / 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.17.3 silently install unpatched bytes; 1.19.0 / 1.21.1 / 1.22.22 fail `Incorrect integrity when fetching from the cache`. v4.0.0 is affected too.
- Merge-conflict markers in yarn.lock (target outside the conflict), H: pass. `--focus` workspace install, H: pass. `yarn audit` on hosted / alias locks: pass. `.yarnclean`, H + vex: pass (1.22.22).
- Hosted rollback on an `integrity sha1-` lock: restores sha512 integrity + npmjs host (documented), frozen install OK: pass (1.10.1).

### Run 9 cells (Linux, `203e092`)
- Patch rewriting the package's own `package.json` (adds a dependency): **fail #591**. Vendored leaves a dangling `dependencies:` entry (offline frozen install fails, lock churns) on 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22. Hosted never installs the new dep, and vex attests (1.10.1 / 1.22.22).
- #493 follow-ups after #520: workspace root `--modules-folder` + non-hoisted members (agent, 1.22.22) and `--install.modules-folder "./my deps"` (agent + vex + frozen-reinstall omission, 1.10.1): pass.
- Agent vex with multiple installed copies across workspaces (#517): pass (1.22.22).
- Repo suites (redirect / vendor / dev-flow, REQUIRED=1): pass on 1.0.2 / 1.7.0 / 1.22.22.
- Superseding hosted patch followed by an in-place frozen install: pass on 1.10.1 / 1.17.3 / 1.22.22. 1.0.2 / 1.7.0 skip the copy only when size+mtime match (yarn limitation, see Known non-bugs).

### Run 10 cells (`045d7ec`)
- Symlinked `yarn.lock` (`yarn.lock -> ../shared/yarn.lock`): hosted refuses (`redirect_symlinked_file_unsupported`); **vendored replaces the link with a regular file, leaving the target unpatched: fail #627** (1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22; npm's `package-lock.json` too). `--dry-run` gives no signal, and rollback doesn't restore the link. yarn itself writes through the link.
- `yarn.lock` file mode 600 / 444 / 755 preserved through H / V scan + rollback: pass (1.22.22).
- Patch that changes an existing dependency range (is-odd `is-number ^6 → ^7`): same as #591 (commented). Vendored leaves `^7.0.0` unpinned, and hosted installs 6.0.0 under a manifest that asks for ^7.
- Agent mode with a `link:` dep: patches the link target outside the project (the code Node loads). Design question, not filed.
- #467 re-checked: still reproduces (H and V, 1.22.22).

## Backlog

1. **Maintainer request (global mode), what's left:** the Windows MSI install of yarn, and a read-only prefix on Windows (Program Files; the runner is admin, so it needs a non-admin user). #437 (1.0.x) is still open. Windows / get-mode / corepack / 1.6.0 / 1.9.4 were covered in run 10.
2. Same-size patched files on yarn ≤1.9 in-place installs: find out which mtime the vendored packer and the Socket hosted tarballs use (the npm 1985 constant would make an upstream→patched same-size change a silent no-op in place).
3. Re-run the v4-only project columns (git dep #363, offline mirror H #364) on macOS/Windows once fixes land; re-check #558 / #519 / #467 once fixed.
4. `vendor --check` / `repair` on a #591-shaped lock (dangling dependency).
5. Other symlinked inputs: `.yarnrc` (offline mirror) and `package.json` (`resolutions`) as symlinks, in H / V / rollback; a symlinked `.socket/` dir.
6. Hosted with a slow or stalled patch API since #581 (connect 10 s / read 60 s): does a stalled hosted tarball download during `yarn install` matter? (that's yarn's own network, so probably n/a)

## Known non-bugs

- `patches-api.socket.dev` isn't used here. Use a local mock API (`--api-url`). The mock must match purls with an unencoded `@` for scoped packages, and vendored runs need `--vendor-source build` plus `blobContent` in the view stub. For hosted `vex` on lock-only checkouts, pass `--patch-server-url <mock>` (CLI_CONTRACT "Patch hosts"); otherwise `package_not_found` is expected.
- **yarn 1.0.2 – 1.6.x install nothing (exit 0, empty node_modules) for `file:` tarball lock entries and offline-mirror installs, even without socket-patch.** Bisected in run 2: Node 10.24.1 / 14.21.3 / 16.20.2 / 22 all behave the same, and 1.7.0 works on all of them. The cause is in yarn, not Node or socket-patch, which is why CI reports `KNOWN LIMITATION` for vendored ≤ 1.6. Not in docs/ecosystems.md.
- An `npm:` alias entry is left unpatched in hosted mode with `redirect_yarn_classic_alias_skipped` (documented), and `vex` omits the package.
- A BOM plus no yarn header comment makes the first entry `entry_not_found`. Yarn always writes the header, so this is synthetic.
- `file:` directory and `link:` deps are skipped by design. (`file:` **tarball** deps are rewired and work.)
- The GitHub shorthand `owner/repo#tag` locks as a codeload tarball and is correctly rewired; only `git+…` patterns are #363.
- Running `scan` from a workspace member dir: vendored → `vendor_lockfile_missing` (exit 1); hosted → exit 0, `redirected: 0`, `redirect_npm_no_lockfile` (npm-only wording). This is the documented hosted refusal posture.
- hosted→agent / vendored→agent keep the existing wiring (`hosted_wiring_retained` / `vendored_ownership_retained`), as documented.
- Concurrent scans: the extras fail with `lock_held` (intended).
- Probe branches can't be deleted from the sandbox (the git proxy rejects ref deletion). Leftovers: `bughunt/yarn-classic/20260930-mirror-git`, `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261001-win-crlf-git`.
- **v5 hosted `rollback` / `remove` need the npm registry.** In the sandbox the CLI's rustls client rejects the TLS-intercepting proxy CA (`error sending request for url (https://registry.npmjs.org/…)`). That's a sandbox artifact. Use a local plain-HTTP registry passthrough with `env -u HTTPS_PROXY -u https_proxy SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. With `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY` set, the restored `resolved` uses `dist.tarball` verbatim (registry.npmjs.org), not registry.yarnpkg.com. That's by design (`npm.rs` `yarn_classic_tarball`).
- v5 vendored mode has no local build (`--vendor-source build` is rejected). The mock must serve a `tarball` artifact from `POST …/patches/package`.
- `scan -g` also reports npm's own bundled deps (npm global root), e.g. `@isaacs/string-locale-compare`. That's correct global discovery.
- Probe branch `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261001-global-mode` is also left on the remote (the proxy blocks deletion).

- Hosted pins are recognized only on `patch.socket.dev` or the `--patch-server-url` / `SOCKET_PATCH_SERVER_URL` origin. With a mock at another origin and no such setting, `rollback` says `Manifest not found` (truly-empty project). Set `SOCKET_PATCH_SERVER_URL=<mock>`.
- Hosted rollback of a lock without `integrity` lines (yarn < 1.10) adds `integrity` lines. That's the "default upstream entry", and yarn 1.7 still installs it frozen.
- Vendored mode on yarn ≤ 1.6 installs nothing. The harness asserts this as a KNOWN LIMITATION (`tests/common/yarn_classic_vex.rs:89`); it's not in the user docs.
- A tarball-URL dependency of the patched name@version is rewired in both modes (it installs patched). Whether a URL "fork" should be refused, as vlt does, is a design question.
- A SIGKILL can leave the lock wired with no `vendor/state.json`. `rollback` then refuses with a remedy, and `repair` / a re-scan rebuild the ledger. That's intended crash handling.
- Hosted rollback ignores the `.yarnrc` `registry` and queries `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY` (default registry.npmjs.org). That's documented (CLI_CONTRACT Hosted unwind / env table). Set `SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY` behind a private registry.
- A nested non-workspace project (its own `yarn.lock` under the root) in hosted mode from the root: `redirect_yarn_classic_entry_not_found`, because hosted reads only the root lock. That's the documented one-project model (run with `--cwd` per project).
- A stale `node_modules` left beside an active `--modules-folder`: Node loads `node_modules` first, so agent patching it is correct.
- Yarn classic never sends `.npmrc` registry auth (host token, bare `_authToken`, `always-auth`, scoped registry, `_auth`) to the hosted patch host, on any release from 1.0.2 to 1.22.22. The berry #404 leak doesn't apply to classic.
- Vendored `vex` attests from the committed artifact even when the installed tree is unpatched (by design, with a `vendored_tree_out_of_sync` warning).
- `scan --vex` in a PnP project exits 1 `manifest_not_found` only because there is nothing to attest. Plain `scan` exits 0 with `yarn_pnp_unsupported`, as pinned by `e2e_safety_yarn_pnp.rs`.
- A platform-skipped optional dep (`fsevents` on Linux) is rewired and attested from the lock pin in hosted mode: the documented lock-only basis, and it installs patched on macOS.
- The mock harness must exclude `node_modules` relative to the package dir, or it serves empty tarballs (a harness bug, not socket-patch).
- yarn classic ignores `YARN_MODULES_FOLDER` / `npm_config_modules_folder` (installs into `node_modules`), so the crawler needn't read them. A `~/.yarnrc` `--modules-folder` resolves relative to `$HOME`, not the project.
- v5 has no `setup` subcommand. Agent cells use `apply`.
- Probe branch `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261002-dev-flow` is also left on the remote (the proxy blocks deletion).
- An `npm:` alias key merged with a direct key in one block isn't something yarn 1.22.22 writes (it emits two blocks), so don't test that shape.
- Hosted rollback on an `integrity sha1-` lock restores a sha512 `integrity` line (the default upstream entry); yarn 1.10 installs it frozen.
- `patch.socket.dev` / `patches-api.socket.dev` are blocked by the sandbox egress proxy, so what the real grant carries (e.g. whether `sha1` is present) can't be checked from here.
- yarn 1.0.x–1.9.x in-place installs skip copying a file whose size and mtime match the installed one (yarn's copy optimisation). With same-length markers and mtime-0 mock tarballs, a superseded patch looks unapplied in place. Fresh installs and 1.10+ are fine. Use different-length markers in harnesses.
- A `.yarnrc` modules-folder that is absolute, or that resolves outside the project, is deliberately ignored by the crawler (fail-closed, `npm_crawler.rs` `resolve_modules_folder`).
- The local mock's batch route must filter by the requested purls, or `scan -g` "finds" packages it never inventoried.
- **macOS probe harness:** the first TCP connects to a freshly started Python mock on a macOS runner stall for 10–30 s. Before #581 the first `scan -g` simply took ~35 s. Since #581's 10 s connect bound, those batches fail (`api_batch_failed` / "All N API batch queries failed", exit 1). This is a harness artifact: warm the mock with a `curl` loop before the first scan. Once warm, `-g` report / agent / vex pass on macOS.
- Agent mode patches a `link:` / `yarn link` dependency's target directory, even outside the project. That's the code Node loads; whether to refuse it is a design question.
- Leftover probe branches (deletion blocked): `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261003-global-rerun`, `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261003-macos-global`.

[agent] 2026-09-30: Yarn classic (1.x) bug-hunt run

This is the first run, so the ledger started empty and there were no `pm:yarn-classic` issues to re-triage.

**Tested:** main `f6b7fb9` (CLI 4.0.0; latest release 4.0.0, also used to check for regressions). Yarn via corepack: 1.0.2, 1.6.0, 1.7.0, 1.9.4, 1.10.1, 1.17.3, 1.22.22 on Node 22 (Linux sandbox). One probe run covered ubuntu, macOS and Windows × 1.10.1 and 1.22.22.

**Setup:** I used a hold-open Python mock of the patch API (batch / by-package / package / view with `blobContent` / hosted tarball in the production URL shape) and patched tarballs built from the real `npm pack` tarballs. Every cell ended with a real `yarn install` on a fresh checkout and a patch-marker check.

## Cells

- **Hosted baseline** (1.0.2, 1.6.0, 1.10.1, 1.22.22; fresh `--frozen-lockfile`): pass.
- **Hosted + `yarn-offline-mirror`:** **fail → #364.** On 1.10+, an online install hits "Integrity check failed" because the mirror's upstream `left-pad-1.3.0.tgz` has the same basename as the hosted URL. `--offline` fails on 1.7+. Linux, macOS and Windows all fail. On 1.7.0 and 1.9.4 an online install passes. 1.0.2 and 1.6.0 are n/a, because they install nothing from a mirror even without socket-patch.
- **Vendored + offline mirror** (1.10.1, 1.22.22; online and `--offline`): pass.
- **Hosted + vendored with a git-sourced dep** (`git+file://…#v1.3.0`): **fail → #363.** The block is rewritten, and yarn then runs git against the tarball, so every install fails ("Command failed" / "spawn ENOTDIR"). The in-run VEX says `not_affected`. Fails on Linux 1.0.2 / 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22 and macOS 1.10.1 / 1.22.22. Windows is blocked (the fixture install couldn't find git).
- **`file:` directory dep:** skipped by both modes, pass. **Remote tarball URL dep:** rewired and installs patched, pass.
- **Hosted workspaces + merged ranges (`^1.3.0`, `1.3.0`, `~1.3.0`) + `resolutions` + scoped package + `npm:` alias** (1.22.22): pass. The alias is skipped with `redirect_yarn_classic_alias_skipped` (documented), and `vex` correctly omits left-pad because of the unpatched alias copy.
- **Vendored, same project** (1.22.22, 1.7.0): pass. It rewires the alias too, and all copies are patched.
- **Hosted CRLF / BOM / BOM+CRLF / headerless locks, then `rollback`** (1.22.22): pass, byte-exact restore.
- **Vendored CRLF / BOM+CRLF, then `vendor --revert`**: pass, byte-exact.
- **Hosted in-place warm reinstall** (1.0.2, 1.10.1, 1.22.22): pass.
- **Re-run idempotency** (hosted and vendored): pass (lock unchanged).
- **Agent `scan --apply` + `setup` postinstall hook, then `yarn add` / `--check-files` / reinstall** (1.0.2, 1.10.1, 1.22.22): pass.
- **Agent mode on nested workspace copies** (version conflict + `nohoist`): pass.

## Issues

- Filed #363: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/363
- Filed #364: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/364

## False positives ruled out

- Scoped packages at first looked "not redirected". That was my mock URL-encoding `@` in purls; the CLI sends it unencoded.
- yarn 1.0.2 and 1.6.0 "exit 0 but nothing installed" from an offline mirror: this happens without socket-patch too (yarn / Node 22), the same family as CI's `KNOWN LIMITATION` for `file:` tarballs on ≤ 1.6.
- A lock with a BOM and **no** yarn header comment misses its first entry (`redirect_yarn_classic_entry_not_found`). Yarn always writes the header, so the lock is synthetic and not filed.
- GitHub-hosted git specs couldn't be fetched through the sandbox proxy, so I used a local `git+file://` repo.

## Probe branches

- `bughunt/yarn-classic/20260930-mirror-git`, run https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/actions/runs/36761888480 (6/6 jobs green; the results are in the RESULT lines).
- **Couldn't delete the branch.** `git push origin --delete` fails through the session git proxy ("remote end hung up"). Sibling routines' probe branches are also still on the remote. A maintainer needs to delete `bughunt/*/2026*` branches.

## Next

1. CI's early-1.x "failing" cells: find out *why* yarn ≤ 1.6 installs nothing from local tarballs or mirrors on modern Node (Node version bisect), and whether socket-patch should refuse vendored mode on those yarns instead of reporting success.
2. Windows: git-sourced dep with git on yarn's PATH, CRLF lock written by yarn on Windows, a path with spaces / unicode for vendored `file:./.socket/…`, and a drive-letter cwd.
3. Hosted ⇄ vendored takeovers and `rollback` on a project with an offline mirror, plus `yarn-offline-mirror-pruning`.
4. `--frozen-lockfile` after `yarn upgrade` / `yarn add` of an unrelated dep on 1.0–1.9 locks (integrity line insertion), and multiple patched versions of one package.
5. VEX on lockfile-only checkouts with aliases and resolutions; `remove` / `repair` / `get <uuid> --mode hosted` on yarn classic.

[agent] 2026-10-01: Yarn classic (1.x) bug-hunt run

**Tested:** main `f6b7fb9`, the same as run 1 (CLI 4.0.0; latest release v4.0.0). Yarn via corepack on Node 22 (Linux sandbox): 1.0.2, 1.6.0, 1.7.0, 1.9.4, 1.10.1, 1.17.3, 1.22.22. For the ≤ 1.6 question I also ran Node 10.24.1, 14.21.3 and 16.20.2. One probe run covered ubuntu, macOS and Windows × 1.7.0, 1.10.1 and 1.22.22. Every cell ended with a real fresh-checkout `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` against a local multi-package mock API (left-pad 1.3.0 + 1.2.0, is-number 7.0.0, @isaacs/string-locale-compare 1.1.0).

## Re-triage
- #363 (git-sourced blocks rewired): **still reproduces.** A new comment adds the Windows cells (1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22 fail in both modes; vendored shows `Couldn't find the binary git`), a real `git+https://github.com/…` spec on Linux, macOS and Windows, and a correction: the GitHub shorthand `owner/repo#tag` locks as a codeload tarball and installs patched. https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/363#issuecomment-5922576899
- #364 (hosted + offline mirror): **still reproduces** on Linux 1.22.22 (`Integrity check failed`). I had nothing new to add, so I didn't comment.

## Cells
- **Multiple patched versions of one package** (workspaces: a→left-pad 1.2.0, b→^1.3.0, plus is-number and a scoped package), hosted and vendored: **pass** on Linux 1.0.2 / 1.6.0 (hosted only) / 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22, and on macOS and Windows 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22 (probe).
- **Takeovers** hosted→vendored and vendored→hosted (`redirect_takeover_reverted_vendored`), each followed by a fresh frozen install and then `rollback`: **pass**. Patched after each takeover, and the lock is restored byte-exact. Linux 1.10.1 / 1.22.22 (local), plus probe macOS and Windows × 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22 and Linux 1.22.22.
- **CRLF lock** (git autocrlf-style), hosted and vendored, then rollback: **pass** on macOS and Windows × 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22 and Linux 1.22.22. CRLF is preserved (0 bare LF) and rollback is byte-exact.
- **`yarn add` of an unrelated dep after scan, then frozen reinstall** (1.7.0, 1.22.22, both modes): **pass**. The wiring is kept and the install is patched.
- **In-place reinstall after scan** (`install --frozen-lockfile`, `install`, `install --check-files`; warm cache) on 1.7.0 / 1.9.4 / 1.10.1 / 1.17.3 / 1.22.22, both modes: **pass**.
- **`yarn check` / `--integrity` / `--verify-tree`** on patched fresh checkouts (1.10.1, 1.22.22, both modes): **pass**.
- **Project path with spaces + unicode** (`sp ace ü/`), both modes, 1.7.0 / 1.22.22 on Linux and all 3 OSes in the probe: **pass**.
- **Scoped package**, hosted on 1.0.2 / 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22 and vendored on 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22: **pass**.
- **`resolved` without a `#sha1` fragment, without `integrity`, or without both**, both modes on 1.22.22: **pass**. Both pins are re-added and the install is patched.
- **Local `file:` tarball dep** (`file:./third/left-pad-1.3.0.tgz`), both modes on 1.10.1 / 1.22.22: **pass**. It is rewired and installs patched.
- **Non-deduplicated lock** (two separate blocks at the same version): **pass**. Both blocks are rewired and rollback is byte-exact.
- **Superseding patch** (a new uuid and new bytes on re-scan), both modes on 1.10.1 / 1.22.22: **pass**. The lock moves to the new uuid, the old vendored artifact dir is removed, the install gets the v2 bytes, and rollback is byte-exact.
- **`remove <purl>`** (hosted `hosted_reverted`, vendored `vendor_reverted`): **pass**. Only that purl's block is reverted. **`repair`**: pass (hosted reports `redirect_only_project`).
- **VEX**: lock-only and installed checkouts with an `npm:` alias + `resolutions` + scoped + multi-version: **pass**. Hosted omits the unpatched alias; vendored attests it. After `yarn upgrade left-pad`, VEX omits the package with `redirect_unwired` / `vendor_unwired`: **pass**.
- **Vendored + `yarn-offline-mirror` (with and without pruning), then install and rollback**, 1.10.1 / 1.22.22: **pass**. Yarn doesn't mirror `file:` tarballs, so the upstream mirror file survives and online and `--offline` installs work after rollback.
- **Concurrent scans** (4 at once, both modes): **pass**. The losers fail with `lock_held`, and the lock and rollback stay intact.
- **hosted→agent / vendored→agent**: documented (`hosted_wiring_retained` / `vendored_ownership_retained`).
- **GitHub shorthand dep** (`stevemao/left-pad#v1.3.0`, a codeload tarball): **pass** in both modes on all 3 OSes.

## Issues
- No new issues filed.
- Commented on #363: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/363#issuecomment-5922576899

## False positives ruled out / findings that aren't bugs
- **Why CI's yarn 1.0.2 / 1.6.0 vendored cells "fail":** I bisected by Node version. Yarn 1.0.2 and 1.6.0 exit 0 and install **nothing** for a `file:` tarball lock entry on Node 10.24.1, 14.21.3, 16.20.2 and 22. Yarn 1.7.0 installs it on all four. The cause is in yarn ≤ 1.6, not in socket-patch and not in Node, which matches CI's comment ("1.7.0 first vendored-capable"). socket-patch can't tell which yarn will run the install from the lock (1.6 and 1.9 locks look the same). This limitation appears only in CI comments, not in docs/ecosystems.md, so a docs note would help. Not filed.
- **Running scan from a workspace member dir** (`cd packages/b`): vendored fails cleanly (`vendor_lockfile_missing`, exit 1). Hosted exits 0 with `redirected: 0` and `redirect_npm_no_lockfile` ("no package-lock.json / npm-shrinkwrap.json present"), whose wording ignores the root `yarn.lock`. That matches the documented "hosted refusals exit 0 + warning" stance, so it's a UX note, not filed.
- **Hosted `vex` on a lock-only checkout said `package_not_found`.** This is documented (CLI_CONTRACT "Patch hosts"): my mock host isn't Socket's patch server. With `--patch-server-url` it attests `(redirected)`.
- The probe's Windows `Couldn't find the binary git` was #363 itself, not a missing git: the control install of the same dep passed in the same job.

## Probe branches
- `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261001-win-crlf-git`, run https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/actions/runs/36798411014 (9/9 jobs green; the script always exits 0, so read the RESULT lines). I read the RESULT lines for Linux 1.22.22, macOS 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22 and Windows 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22. The ubuntu 1.7.0 / 1.10.1 jobs were not read, so this run makes no probe claims for those two cells.
- **Couldn't delete the branch** (`git push --delete` → "remote end hung up" through the session git proxy, same as run 1). A maintainer needs to delete `bughunt/yarn-classic/20260930-mirror-git` and `bughunt/yarn-classic/20261001-win-crlf-git`.

## Next
1. `.yarnrc` / `package.json` signals of yarn ≤ 1.6 (`yarn-path`, `packageManager: yarn@1.6.0`, `engines.yarn`): does vendored mode warn? If a pinned yarn ≤ 1.6 project gets `status: success` and then installs nothing, decide whether that's worth a docs or refusal issue.
2. Interrupted runs (SIGKILL mid-rewrite) and recovery via a re-run or `rollback`; `--dry-run` byte-identity on CRLF / BOM locks.
3. `get <uuid> --mode vendored` / `--mode hosted` for one version of a multi-version package; `scan --prune` / `--sync` on yarn classic after `yarn remove`.
4. Yarn 1.22.x `.yarnrc` `--install.frozen-lockfile true`, `--pure-lockfile`, and `yarn import` locks (converted from package-lock).
5. `optionalDependencies` / platform-skipped packages (lock-only entries) in both modes and in VEX.

[agent] 2026-10-01: maintainer note: test global (`-g`) mode for hosted patches

This is a maintainer request, not a run report. Add it to the top of the backlog and keep it there until the cells below are covered.

**Ask:** make sure we correctly scan global installs when `-g` / `--global` is passed, on every major Yarn classic (1.x) version and on Linux, macOS and Windows.

**Where Yarn classic (1.x) puts global installs:** `yarn global add`; discovery via `yarn global dir`. Cover a custom `--global-folder` / `prefix` in .yarnrc, and yarn installed via npm, corepack and the Windows MSI.

**What to check** (prove each with a real global install, not by reading source):
1. `socket-patch scan -g` (no `--mode`) is report-only. It must find every globally installed Yarn classic (1.x) package that has a hosted patch: none missing, no project packages leaking in, correct versions. Also check `--json`.
2. `scan -g` run from inside a Yarn classic (1.x) project versus outside one: `-g` must scan only the global location, and a scan without `-g` must never touch it.
3. `scan -g --mode hosted` and `scan --global-prefix <dir> --mode hosted` must refuse loudly, as designed ("global installs have no project lockfile to redirect"). They must exit non-zero and write nothing.
4. `get -g` defaults to agent mode. Check `scan -g --apply`, `apply -g`, `rollback -g` and `vex -g`: the globally installed copy is actually patched (run the installed tool or import it), rollback restores it byte for byte, and `vex` only attests what's applied.
5. `--global-prefix <dir>` and `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1` behave the same as `-g`. That covers custom prefixes, version managers, paths with spaces or unicode, and a non-root user's prefix.
6. A global directory you can't write to (root-owned prefix, Windows Program Files) must fail loudly with a clear error, never exit 0 unpatched.

Add OS × Yarn classic (1.x) version cells for `-g` (scan report / apply / rollback) to the coverage matrix, and use probe branches for macOS and Windows.

Work around it with a local plain-HTTP passthrough and `env -u HTTPS_PROXY -u https_proxy SOCKET_NPM_REGISTRY=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. With that env set, the restorer writes `dist.tarball` verbatim (registry.npmjs.org) instead of registry.yarnpkg.com, which is expected.

- #363 (git-sourced blocks rewired): **still reproduces** on v5. New: hosted `rollback` reports success but "restores" the git block to the registry tarball, so installs keep failing. Comment: https://github.com/SocketDev/socket-patch/issues/363#issuecomment-5926333522

- **Global mode (maintainer checklist)**, `yarn global add left-pad is-number`:
  - `scan -g` report-only finds the yarn-global packages, both inside and outside a project. There's no leakage either way: a scan without `-g` reports only the project, and the project lock is untouched. **pass** on Linux / macOS × 1.10.1 / 1.22.22.
  - `scan -g --mode hosted`, `--global-prefix … --mode hosted` and `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1 --mode hosted` all exit 2 and write nothing: **pass** on every OS and version.
  - `scan -g --mode agent` / `get <uuid> -g` patch the real global copy (`require()` works), `vex -g` attests only the applied copies (dropping one manually removes it from subcomponents), and `rollback -g` / `--global-prefix` rollback are byte-exact. `SOCKET_GLOBAL=1` behaves the same. **pass** on Linux (sandbox + CI) and macOS × 1.10.1 / 1.22.22.

  - **`get -g --mode hosted|vendored` and `scan -g --mode vendored` → filed #436.** They rewrite the cwd project's yarn.lock, exit 0 and leave the global copy unpatched. Reproduces on all 3 OSes × 1.0.2 / 1.10.1 / 1.22.22. v4.0.0 behaves the same, so it's not a v5 regression.
